full_source_original_object.report:
MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Echogenic mass seen laterally in the right knee on ultrasound. Suggest for MRI evaluation.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
No prior imaging available for evaluation.

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No definite meniscal tear, no evidence of para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is slightly laterally subluxed. Lateral trochlear inclination angle is borderline, measuring approximately 11 degrees. TT TG distance is not increased. Insall Salvati ratio is 1.4, which is also within normal range. Thickening of the lateral retinaculum may be due to prior subluxation. Increased fat attenuation is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.

Fluid

Small joint effusion is seen. No loose body. Small Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss most observable at the lateral patella facet and apex associated subchondral chondral edema. Chondral irregularity at the trochlea is also seen associated with subchondral cysts.


Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Increasing fat signal is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.
Otherwise no focal soft tissue mass detected at the knee.

Severe chondral loss at the patellofemoral compartment particularly involving the lateral patella facet and apex associated with marked subchondral edema and subchondral cysts at both the femoral trochlea and patella. Patella is slightly laterally subluxed with borderline lateral trochlear inclination angle but normal Insall Salvati ratio and TT TG distance.

Chondropathie modérée au compartiment antérieur et légère au compartiment interne et externe.

See above.

Normal.

Clinical information:
Severe edema of the medial condyle of left knee.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated <[Date]> of <[Month]> <[YEAR]>

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intra since degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Findings are ready seen on prior study but appears more degenerate. Several para meniscal cysts are seen at the posterior aspect of the meniscus measuring up to 0.4 cm in size. Meniscal extrusion approximately 0.6 cm noted.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A large subchondral cysts are seen at the posterior superior aspect of the tibial plateau, very much larger than prior study. Moderate degenerative changes multiple osteophytes are seen, most significant at the medial tibiofemoral joint. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis..

Medial compartment: Focal full-thickness chondral loss measuring up to 1.3 cm in size associated subchondral edema. Moderate chondrosis in the rest of the femoral condyle Findings have slightly progressed compared to prior study.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondral irregularity. No significant subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, similar to previous. Interval increase in degenerative changes of the meniscus is observed. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.6 cm is seen. Multiple para meniscal cysts are also present.

Interval increase in degenerative changes are identified evident as shown by increased osteophytes, full-thickness chondral loss at the medial tibiofemoral joint associated increasing subchondral edema, and multiple enlarging subchondral cysts at the posterior medial tibial plateau.

full_source_original_object.report:
LEFT KNEE MRI 

CLINICAL INDICATION: Medial meniscus injury, query MCL tear

Technique: Multiplanar PD, PF fat sat and T1 imaging was acquired through the knee. 

Comparison: The x-ray [Date]

Findings:

General:
Marrow:  There is edema of the medial femoral condyle at the site of the MCL insertion, and in the posterolateral femoral condyle. There is edema in the medial proximal tibia and the posterolateral proximal tibia.
Consistent with internal bone contusion secondary valgus injury.
Effusion:  No significant effusion

Menisci:   
Medial meniscus:   Intact.
Lateral meniscus:   Intact.

Ligaments and tendons:
Cruciate ligaments:   There is increased signal in the PCL, which may be keeping with a low-grade tear. No tibial translation.
Medial collateral ligament:   High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal of the mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the meniscal femoral as well as posterior plate components of the deep medial collateral ligament.
Lateral collateral ligament:   normal
Popliteofibular ligament:   normal
Other posterolateral corner ligaments:   normal
Popliteal tendon:   normal
Iliotibial band:   normal

Extensor mechanism:
Quadriceps tendon: Mild increased signal along the patellar insertion, in keeping with tendinosis
Patella:   normal
Patellar tendon:   normal
Hoffa?s fat pad: Subtle edema in keeping with impingement

Cartilage:
Patellofemoral joint: Mild chondrosis mainly along the trochlear aspect there
Medial compartment:   normal cartilage
Lateral compartment:  Mild chondrosis.

CONCLUSION:

1. Intact menisci.
2. High-grade partial thickness tear of the medial collateral ligament and bone contusions posterior lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau in keeping with valgus injury.
3. Mild chondrosis.
4. Mild quadriceps tendinosis without tear.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS


> Increased interstitial signal of distal quadriceps tendon on F/S T2WI and incrased fat stranding over anterior suprapatellar fat pad, R/O grade 1 injury and suprapatellar fat pad inflammation.
> Suspicious of mild increased singal intensity of patellar articular cartialge on F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 chondromalacia.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to contusion or peripheral vascularity.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Minimal joint effusion and suprapatellar plica.

Impression: 
1. Grade 1 injury of distal quadriceps tendon and anterior suprapatellar fat pad inflammation.
2. R/O grade 1 patellar chondromalacia.
3. No strong evidence of full thickness tear of ACL.
4. R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to contusion or peripheral vascularity.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

full_source_original_object.report:
MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Right knee instability. Anterior drawer test positive? Anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Mild hyperintensity is seen at the posterior horn suggestive of intrasubstance degeneration. No definite tear. No parameniscal cyst. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Intact fibers are present however caliber of these fibers is somewhat attenuated compatible with a remote low-grade partial thickness injury. No significant tibial translation.

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Marked patella chondral hypertrophy is seen measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. It appears heterogeneously hyperintense with regions of hypointensity, possibly due to mineralization. No evidence of invasion into the patella bone. It is closely abutting a medial plica. A possible loose body is also seen. Suspicious fissure also observed at the apex. Findings non specific in nature but favours to represent severe chondromalacia. Differential diagnoses such as focal synovitis and PVNS are less probable. 

Medial compartment: Mild chondrosis of the medial femoral condyle.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondrosis of the lateral femoral condyle.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Low grade, remote, partial thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No tibial translation.

Marked heterogeneous hypertrophy of the articular cartilage of the patella measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. Signal in this irregular thickened cartilage is heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging and shows focal regions of hypointensity which may represent mineralization. Findings are favored to represent severe chondropathic change involving the articular cartilage of the patella.
